about: What a Hanzo IAM access token says about its bearer, as data both readers test against:
this package (claims_vectors_test.go) and hanzoai/datastore's IAM user directory, which
embeds this file from its contrib/authz submodule (src/Access/tests/gtest_iam_verifier.cpp).
claims  the payload IAM signs (a reader adds iss, aud, exp around it). `owner` is present
on purpose and never decides anything: IAM stamps the APPLICATION's org into it.
kid     the signing key the token names.
org     the tenant the bearer acts in: the first entry of `orgs`, empty for none. Claims.Home.
person  a human: not a program, and a non-empty membership set. !Claims.Machine.
superadmin  person AND org == "admin" AND kid == superadmin_kid. What the datastore grants.
sudo    what Claims.Sudo answers: a person with "admin" anywhere in `orgs`, any key.
Where superadmin and sudo differ, the two readers disagree about platform authority; the
datastore is the narrower one (superadmin implies sudo, never the reverse).

cases.name: person signing in through their own org's application
person signing in through an application the admin org owns: owner is the app's org
person signing in through another org's shared application
person in several orgs acts in the first, their home
token without a membership set has no org and is no person
empty membership set is the same as none
SuperAdmin: home org admin, signed with the admin org's key
home org admin signed with another org's key is not SuperAdmin
operator anchored in a brand org with an admin membership is not SuperAdmin
a look-alike of the reserved org is an ordinary org
program of the admin org: no org of its own, never SuperAdmin
program granted a membership acts in that org
program granted the admin org is still never SuperAdmin
first membership naming no org leaves the bearer without one
